title: Phase 7A - Sustainable Computing Evaluation of Adaptive Pruning
status: written before any Phase-7A model was built, recovered or measured

questions.primary: Can the layer-wise adaptive pruning policy reduce measured CPU inference energy while preserving predictive accuracy?
questions.secondary: Does the adaptive policy provide a better energy-accuracy trade-off than uniform structured pruning and a strong non-RL structured baseline (LAMP-derived)?

positioning: Deployment realization: the thesis PPO policies were unstructured masks, which do not reduce dense CPU work. Their per-unit pruning ratios are realized here as physical structured channel removal. No claim is made that the masked thesis models themselves reduce latency or energy.

methods.dense: frozen Phase-2 dense reference, recovered with the same protocol (identity policy)
methods.ppo: most frequent Phase-5 C1 selected policy over policy seeds 500-519 (ties: smallest action vector)
methods.uniform: one common ratio for all four units on a 0.001 grid minimizing |MACs - MACs_PPO| (MAC matching, fixed before results; ties: smallest ratio). Exact matching is limited by integer channel counts; the residual gap is recorded and reported
methods.lamp: Phase-6 LAMP mask at exactly PPO's zero count; thesis-unit sparsity = zeros / weights, realized with the same structured rule

structured_rule.code: src/pruning/structured_units.py and src/pruning/structured.py (validated in Paper 3, unchanged)
structured_rule.keep: max(1, round((1 - r) * C)) channels with the largest L1 norm, scored on the dense model
structured_rule.resnet8_mapping: Approximate realization: thesis units stage2/stage3 pruned all weights of a stage (conv1, conv2, shortcut), whereas the validated structured units remove block-internal channels only (stage output widths are not pruned); thesis unit 'stem' (conv1 weights) maps to the coupled stage-1 residual width.
integrity_checks_before_measurement: slimmed model contains no pruning masks or reparameterizations
parameter counts equal the analytic values
conv/linear MACs equal the analytic values
slimmed vs masked-equivalent logits agree within 1e-4 (Paper-3 tolerance) on a fixed batch
state dict saved, reloaded into a fresh skeleton, identical logits

recovery.protocol: frozen Phase-6 fine-tuning protocol as used in Paper 3 (Adam lr 1e-4, betas 0.9/0.999, eps 1e-8, wd 0, cosine to 0 per epoch, batch 128, random crop pad 4 + horizontal flip, BN train mode in training, eval mode for evaluation)
recovery.selection: model after the final epoch; no selection

accuracy.primary_metric: VAL-RL accuracy (2,500 images, Phase-5 split) after recovery
accuracy.reference: recovered dense model (identity policy, same protocol)
accuracy.preservation_rule: |A_method - A_dense_recovered| <= 0.5 percentage points on VAL-RL; otherwise the model is classified as not accuracy-preserving (threshold fixed, never changed)
accuracy.test_set: not used (no frozen test protocol exists for these new structured models)
accuracy.known_bias: the PPO policies were trained with VAL-RL rewards and selected on VAL-SELECT, so PPO's validation accuracy may be optimistically biased relative to the baselines

energy.backend: Intel RAPL package energy (\Energy Meter(RAPL_Package0_PKG)\Energy) via the Windows Energy Meter Interface, read with PDH raw values; units picowatt-hours (1 pWh = 3.6e-9 J); ~1 ms refresh. Secondary domain: RAPL_Package0_PP0 (cores). DRAM is not exposed on this machine. No TDP or software estimate is used
energy.primary_metric: E_1000 = package joules / N * 1000 for one contiguous block of N inferences
secondary_metrics: net package energy above the session's idle package power (30 s idle measured at session start)
energy.energy_saving: 100 * (1 - E_method / E_dense) with the dense anchor of the same session

workload.excluded: model construction, checkpoint loading and warm-up

energy.session_design: one fresh process per (architecture, session); the 4 models of the architecture (dense anchor included) in a seeded random order per session

conditions.ac_power: required (the script refuses to measure on battery)
conditions.power_plan: logged; must be identical in every session
conditions.cpu_affinity: logical CPU 2 (P-core), set before torch import
conditions.cpu_load_gate: system CPU load <= 15% over 5 s before each session

pilot.purpose: stability of readings only; dense models only, so no pruned-model outcome is seen
pilot.design: 2 fresh processes per architecture, each 1,000 warm-up then 3 consecutive dense blocks of N
pilot.rule: if the coefficient of variation of dense E_1000 over the 6 blocks is <= 3% for both architectures, use N = 100,000; otherwise double N once and repeat the pilot; if still > 3%, stop and report that the energy readings are not stable enough

latency_and_compute.latency: median per-inference time (perf_counter_ns) over the same N inferences
latency_and_compute.speedup: dense median / method median within a session
latency_and_compute.params_macs: analytic, verified against the built model
latency_and_compute.edp: E_per_inference * median latency, normalized to the same-session dense anchor; not a carbon metric
latency_and_compute.storage: size of the saved state dict

statistics.summary: per method: median, mean, SD and IQR over 5 sessions of E_1000, latency, paired saving vs dense
statistics.paired_test_vs_dense: exact one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 5 paired E_1000 values (H1: method < dense); with n = 5 the smallest attainable p is 0.031, so p-values are secondary
statistics.paired_tests_between_methods: exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 5 session pairs (smallest attainable p 0.0625); reported descriptively
statistics.noise_threshold: 2 x the between-session coefficient of variation of the dense anchor's E_1000
statistics.consistent_energy_reduction: lower E_1000 than the same-session dense anchor in 5 of 5 sessions AND median paired saving > noise threshold
statistics.stop_rule: if a method's median saving lies within the noise threshold, its energy result is reported as not distinguishable from session noise

primary_success_criterion: Case A for an architecture: PPO-Structured satisfies the 0.5 pp preservation rule AND shows a consistent energy reduction versus dense

interpretation_cases.A: PPO preserves accuracy and consistently reduces energy: 'The structured deployment realization of the adaptive pruning policy reduces measured CPU inference energy while preserving predictive performance.'
interpretation_cases.B: consistent energy reduction but > 0.5 pp loss: 'The policy reduces operational energy, but the observed saving comes with a measurable accuracy trade-off.'
interpretation_cases.C: accuracy preserved but no consistent energy reduction: 'Accuracy-preserving structured pruning did not translate into measurable energy savings on this CPU.'
interpretation_cases.D: a baseline is more energy-efficient than PPO at comparable accuracy: stated transparently

method_comparison_rule.baseline_better: comparable accuracy and baseline E_1000 lower than PPO's in 5 of 5 sessions, or baseline accuracy higher by > 0.5 pp with median E_1000 not higher than PPO's
method_comparison_rule.ppo_better: the same conditions with the roles exchanged
method_comparison_rule.otherwise: no clear difference in the energy-accuracy trade-off

projection: deployment-scale savings for 1e6, 1e7, 1e8 inferences = (E_dense - E_method) per inference x N, in kWh; labelled a projection; no CO2e conversion
claims_policy: no 'green', 'environmentally friendly', 'carbon-neutral' or carbon-footprint wording; allowed: energy-efficient inference, reduced operational inference energy
known_before_registration: Paper-3 batch-1 latency tables already contain the action-grid shapes of the PPO policies; no Phase-7A energy, accuracy or latency value had been measured
